title: Sell Mineral Rights in Meshoppen, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Meshoppen, PA | Wyoming County
metaDescription: Meshoppen, PA sits along the Susquehanna in Wyoming County's dry-gas Marcellus core. We buy mineral rights directly with straight talk on royalty deductions.
heroLead: Meshoppen sits right where Meshoppen Creek meets the Susquehanna River, in a corner of Wyoming County that turned out to be some of the best dry-gas Marcellus rock in the entire play.
intro: Wyoming County doesn't carry the liquids-rich production of the southwestern counties, this is dry gas territory, methane straight through, and it's some of the most productive dry-gas Marcellus rock anywhere in Pennsylvania. If your family has held ground around Meshoppen for generations, there's a real chance a lease from the early Marcellus years is still producing on your family's land today.
We buy mineral and royalty interests around Meshoppen directly. We're familiar with how dry-gas leases in this county were typically structured and what to look for in your specific paperwork.

sections.heading: Dry Gas Changes the Math
paragraphs: Without natural gas liquids to separate out, dry-gas production around Meshoppen generally sees fewer processing deductions than wet-gas wells farther southwest, though gathering and compression fees still apply. That's a real structural difference worth understanding when you're comparing your royalty check to what a friend in Washington County might describe.

Wyoming County has been one of the more consistently active dry-gas counties in the state, with operators running large multi-well pads that pull acreage from well beyond Meshoppen borough itself into surrounding Meshoppen Township.

sections.heading: River-Bottom Farms and Old Family Deeds
paragraphs: A lot of the land along the Susquehanna near Meshoppen was farmed by the same families for generations before leasing began, and those older deeds sometimes use river-bottom boundary descriptions that take care to match against modern parcel lines. We handle that title work through the Wyoming County Recorder of Deeds in Tunkhannock.
If your interest passed down through several generations without a formal mineral deed ever being recorded separately, that's common here and something we can work through with you.

sections.heading: Reading a Dry-Gas Royalty Statement
paragraphs: We'll go through your actual statements with you before discussing any number, so you understand your decimal interest, your allocated production, and exactly what's being deducted and why.

faqs.question: Is dry gas worth less than wet gas?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. Pricing depends on the gas market itself, and dry gas avoids some of the liquids-processing deductions that wet-gas production carries, so the comparison isn't as simple as one being better than the other.

faqs.question: My family's lease is old, from the early Marcellus years. Does that matter?
faqs.answer: It can. Older leases sometimes lack royalty protections that later leases include, so we review your lease terms specifically rather than assuming.

faqs.question: Do you buy interests along the river-bottom farms specifically?
faqs.answer: Yes, we regularly buy interests tied to river-bottom tracts around Meshoppen and Meshoppen Township, including ones with older, less formal title histories.
